changes.reason: Analytic s,p orbitals on each carbon (8 functions, the same count as now) seed atom-centred functions that do not depend on the pseudopotential, so no column ends up in the vacuum.
SMV needs iterations to minimise Omega_I during disentanglement; the value carried over from SCDM is 0.

diagnosis: This is a 2D two-carbon layer with 16 Å of vacuum along c. The 8 functions are the four s,p functions on each carbon. That means 4 occupied valence bands and 4 functions taken from the entangled conduction states. Below E_F those are the pi* and sigma* bands, which are mixed with the vacuum states that start around +4 eV. The SCDM default from the protocol (mu = -30.7 eV, sigma = 11.8 eV) comes from a poor projectability fit (residual 0.245). Its weight favours the low-lying vacuum states over sigma*, so the column selection put function 7 in the vacuum at z = -7.9 Å, 8.03 Å from any atom. It has spread 5.4 Å². Function 6 is also pulled 2.24 Å off the plane, with spread 5.7 Å². These two diffuse functions carry about 48 % of the hopping weight beyond r_c. That is why eta_2 is 6.2 meV untruncated but 30.2 meV after truncation. The decay length is 2.3 Å, and the error after truncation sits in valence bands 3-5 near E_F. The localisation step converged monotonically, so the problem is not the gauge minimisation: SCDM chose the wrong subspace, and no setting of its knobs makes sigma* outweigh the vacuum states. PDWF, the other family that has been tried, keeps its centres on the atoms, but its projectability-threshold freezing gave eta_2 of 60-66 meV whatever its two thresholds were set to. SMV with analytic s,p trial orbitals and a smooth Omega_I-minimising subspace selection is the family that hasn't been tried.
